title: kv-cache: adaptive eviction & spillover memory manager (defrag + paging) v20
author: Aisha Khan
ci_status: perf: pass (kv-cache p99 latency -3% on long-tail workloads)
description: Background: observed KV cache memory fragmentation and paging under sustained multi-tenant long-context workloads causing higher p99 latency and increased GPU memory churn. Motivation: improve tail latency and reduce OOMs by making eviction and spillover policies adaptive to fragmentation, hot-key locality, and kernel-friendly alignment. Overview of changes: 1) Introduce a spillover memory manager that separates small-fragment allocation pools from large contiguous pages and prefers compaction when fragmentation exceeds threshold. 2) Adaptive eviction priority that combines recency, token-weighted size, and fragmentation penalty to avoid thrashing of large KV entries. 3) Paging improvements: lazy paging for cold prefixes, coalesced page writes for NVME-backed spillover, and prefetch hints for incoming batched requests. 4) Defragmentation: background coalescing job with rate limiting tied to SLO (does not run when p50 latency > configured threshold). 5) Scheduler/kernel hints: align key chunk sizes to 128B/4KB boundaries to improve kernel memory copy performance and reduce PCIe transfers. 6) Telemetry: added metrics for fragmentation ratio, compaction runs, pages read/written, and eviction score distribution. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind feature flag (runtime.kv.adaptive_eviction=v20) with Canary in Dedicated pool -> 10% -> 50% -> global. Backwards compat: spill files format is backwards-compatible; migration path handled by new manager on first startup. Testing: unit tests for eviction scoring, integration tests with synthetic long-context traces, perf runs across small/medium/large instances showing 2-5% p99 latency improvement and ~12% reduction in GPU memory churn on high-fragmentation scenarios. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-2345) - [x] unit tests added - [x] integration & perf runs complete - [x] telemetry dashboards updated - [x] feature flag gated - [x] canary rollout plan prepared

review_comments: Devansh Rao (2026-02-12): Great direction. Two asks: 1) please add a guard so defrag doesn't run during GC-heavy windows; 2) add a dashboard panel for eviction score distribution. Response: added a rate-limited defrag guard tied to p50 SLO and pushed eviction_score histogram metric.

Liam O'Connor (2026-02-14): Can you justify the 4KB alignment choice? Will it regress small-token workloads? Response: 4KB/128B alignment are heuristics -- small-token workloads use the small-fragment pool which keeps 128B buckets; added microbenchmarks showing no regression on small-token latency and improved memcpy throughput for large transfers.
Maria Gomez (2026-02-16): NVME spill files format looks fine but add version header for future evolution. Response: added file header with version field and migration tests.
release_notes: Improved KV cache memory management: adaptive eviction that reduces thrash on large-key workloads; background defragmentation with rate limiting; smarter paging & coalesced spillover writes; new telemetry for fragmentation and eviction scoring. Result: lower p99 latency and fewer OOMs under long-context multi-tenant workloads.
testing_summary: Unit tests: eviction scoring and allocator; Integration: long-context synthetic traces; Perf: +2-5% p99 improvement on stressed fragmentation scenarios; Canary rollout plan passed Dedicated canary with telemetry observed.
notes: Follow-up work tracked in ENG-2987: GPU-side kernel memcpy optimizations for spill reads and tighter batching interaction to further reduce p99 latency under mixed short/long workloads.
